recipes.name: Badam milk
instructions: Soak 15 almonds in hot water for 30 minutes, then peel them.
Grind the almonds with a little milk to form a smooth paste.
Heat 2 cups of milk in a pan until it comes to a boil.
Stir in the almond paste and mix well.
Add 2 tablespoons of sugar and stir until it dissolves.
Add cardamom powder and saffron strands for aroma and color.
Let it cook on low heat for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add a pinch of turmeric and ½ teaspoon of rose water.
Pour into two glasses, garnish with chopped nuts, and serve warm or chilled.

recipes.name: chicken dum biryani
ingredients: A handful of chopped coriander & mint leaves
2 large onions (thinly sliced and fried until golden brown)
¼ cup milk + a pinch of saffron
Extra coriander & mint leaves for garnish
instructions: In a bowl, mix chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, spices, lemon juice, and oil.
Add chopped mint, coriander, and slit green chilies.
Cover and marinate for at least 1 hour (preferably overnight for better flavor).
In a large pot, boil water with bay leaves, cardamoms, cloves, cinnamon, cumin, and salt.
Add the soaked rice and cook until it's 70% done (grains should still be firm).
Drain the rice and set aside.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, spread the marinated chicken at the bottom.
Layer half of the partially cooked rice over the chicken.
Sprinkle fried onions, saffron milk, chopped coriander, mint, and ghee.
Repeat with the remaining rice and top it with the rest of the garnish.
Seal the pot with foil and cover with a lid.
Cook on low flame for 30-40 minutes (place a griddle/tava underneath for even heating).
Gently mix the biryani before serving.
Serve hot with raita and salad.

recipes.name: chicken fry
ingredients: 1 tbsp rice flour (optional, for extra crispiness)
instructions: In a bowl, mix chicken with ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, red chili powder, garam masala, black pepper, lemon juice, salt, and yogurt.
Add corn flour, rice flour, and egg (if using) to coat the chicken well.
Let it marinate for at least 1 hour (preferably overnight for better flavor).
In a deep pan, heat oil over medium heat.
Once the oil is hot, add the marinated chicken pieces in batches.
Fry on medium heat until golden brown and crispy.
Add curry leaves and green chilies in the last 2 minutes for extra aroma.
Remove the fried chicken and place it on a paper towel to remove excess oil.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and onion rings.

recipes.name: chicken noodles
ingredients: 200g noodles (egg noodles or any preferred type)
instructions: Boil water in a pot, add a little salt and a few drops of oil.
Add the noodles and cook as per package instructions.
Drain and rinse under cold water to prevent sticking. Set aside.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan.
Add minced garlic and ginger, sauté until fragrant.
Add sliced chicken, season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Stir-fry until fully cooked. Remove from the pan and set aside.
In the same pan, add 1 tbsp oil.
Sauté onions, capsicum, carrot, and cabbage for 2 minutes.
Add soy sauce, chili sauce, vinegar, and black pepper. Mix well.
Add the cooked chicken and boiled noodles to the pan.
Toss everything well to coat with the sauces.
Stir-fry for another 2-3 minutes.
Sprinkle chopped spring onions on top.
Serve hot with extra soy sauce or chili sauce on the side.

recipes.name: chiken berger
ingredients: 250g minced chicken (or boneless chicken breast, ground)
½ tsp paprika or red chili powder (optional, for spice)
½ tsp oregano or mixed herbs
instructions: In a bowl, mix minced chicken with ginger-garlic paste, salt, pepper, paprika, oregano, soy sauce, and lemon juice.
Add breadcrumbs and an egg for binding, then mix well.
Shape the mixture into round, flat patties.
Let them rest for 10-15 minutes in the fridge (helps them hold shape).
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Cook the chicken patty for 4-5 minutes on each side until golden brown and fully cooked.
Preheat the grill and brush it with a little oil.
Grill each patty for about 5 minutes per side.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Bake for 20 minutes, flipping halfway.
Toast the burger buns lightly.

recipes.name: Daddojanam
ingredients: 1 cup cooked rice (preferably soft and slightly mushy)
¼ cup milk (optional, to adjust consistency)
instructions: Cook 1 cup of rice with extra water to make it soft and slightly mushy.
Let it cool slightly before mixing (warm rice absorbs curd well).
Mash the rice lightly.
Add curd and milk, then mix well to get a creamy consistency.
Add salt and mix thoroughly.
Heat oil or ghee in a small pan.
Add mustard seeds and let them splutter.
Add cumin seeds, chopped green chili, grated ginger, dry red chili, and curry leaves.
Sauté for a few seconds until fragrant.
Pour the tempering over the curd rice and mix well.
Garnish with coriander leaves and pomegranate seeds.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.
Best served with pickle, papad, or fried green chilies.
Can be enjoyed as a cooling meal during hot summers.

recipes.name: fish fry
ingredients: 500g fish (pomfret, kingfish, or any firm fish)
1 tbsp corn flour (optional, for extra crunch)
instructions: Wash the fish thoroughly with water and pat it dry. If using whole fish, make slits for better marination.

In a bowl, mix ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, black pepper, lemon juice, salt, rice flour, and corn flour. Add little water if needed to make a thick paste.
Coat the fish evenly with the marinade and let it rest for at least 30 minutes (or overnight for better flavor).
Heat oil in a pan on medium flame. Place the marinated fish and fry until golden brown on both sides. Flip gently to avoid breaking.
Garnish with fried curry leaves and serve with lemon wedges and onion rings.

recipes.name: French-Style Curry Chicken
ingredients: 500g boneless chicken (thighs or breast), cut into pieces
1 tbsp curry powder (mild, like Madras curry)
½ cup white wine (optional, for depth of flavor)
1 cup heavy cream or crème fraîche
½ cup chicken stock (if needed for consistency)
Fresh parsley or coriander for garnish
Steamed rice, mashed potatoes, or baguette
instructions: Heat butter or olive oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add the chopped onions and sauté until soft and translucent.
Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another minute.
Add the chicken pieces and cook until lightly browned on all sides.
Sprinkle the curry powder and turmeric (if using) over the chicken.
Stir well to coat the chicken with the spices.
Pour in the white wine and let it simmer for 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced.
Lower the heat and stir in the Dijon mustard and heavy cream.
If the sauce is too thick, add some chicken stock to adjust consistency.
Simmer for 5-7 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is rich.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish with fresh parsley or coriander.
Serve hot with steamed rice, mashed potatoes, or a crusty French baguette.

recipes.name: kesari
ingredients: 2 cups water (or milk for a richer taste)
A pinch of saffron strands (soaked in 2 tbsp warm water or milk)
A few drops of orange/yellow food color (optional)
instructions: Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a pan and roast cashews and raisins until golden. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining ghee to the pan, then add semolina (rava).
Roast on low-medium heat for 5-7 minutes, stirring constantly, until aromatic. Do not brown.
In a separate pot, heat 2 cups water (or milk) and bring it to a gentle boil.
Slowly pour the hot water into the roasted semolina while stirring continuously to prevent lumps.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until the mixture thickens.
Add sugar, soaked saffron, and cardamom powder. Mix well.
Stir and cook for 3-4 minutes until the sugar dissolves and the mixture becomes glossy.
If using food color, add a few drops at this stage.
Add the fried cashews and raisins. Mix well.
Turn off the heat and let it rest for 2 minutes before serving.
Serve warm as a sweet treat or dessert.

recipes.name: gulab jamun
ingredients: 1 cup khoya (mawa), crumbled (or ½ cup milk powder)
1 tsp rose water or kewra water (optional, for aroma)
A few saffron strands (optional, for color & flavor)
instructions: In a wide pan, add sugar and water.
Heat on medium flame, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Add cardamom, saffron, and rose water/kewra water.
Simmer for 5 minutes until slightly sticky (but not too thick).
Turn off the heat and keep warm.
Prepare the Gulab Jamun Dough
In a bowl, mix khoya, all-purpose flour, semolina, and baking soda.
Add ghee and mix well.
Slowly add milk (a little at a time) and knead a soft, smooth dough (not sticky).
Cover and rest for 10 minutes.
Shape the Gulab Jamuns
Divide the dough into small, smooth balls (around 12-15).
Ensure there are no cracks to prevent breaking while frying.
Fry the Gulab Jamuns
In a deep pan, heat ghee or oil on low-medium heat.
Test with a small piece of dough  it should rise slowly without browning too fast.
Gently drop gulab jamuns into the oil.
Fry on low heat, stirring gently for even cooking.
Cook until golden brown (about 6-8 minutes).
Remove and drain excess oil.
Soak in Sugar Syrup
Drop the hot gulab jamuns into the warm sugar syrup (not boiling).
Let them absorb syrup for at least 2-3 hours for the best texture.

recipes.name: Milk kova
ingredients: Full-fat milk 1 liter (for about 200g of khoya)
instructions: Boil the Milk: Pour the full-fat milk into a heavy-bottomed pan and bring it to a boil over medium heat.
Simmer and Reduce: Lower the heat and continue stirring frequently to prevent burning. Keep scraping the sides and mixing the thickened milk back in.
Thickening Process: As the milk thickens, reduce the heat further and stir continuously to avoid sticking.
Final Consistency: When the milk turns into a grainy, semi-solid mass and stops releasing moisture, your khoya is ready.
Cooling & Storing: Allow it to cool completely before storing in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

recipes.name: Ragi Sangati
ingredients: ½ cup rice (optional for texture, but commonly added)
instructions: Rinse the rice and cook it with 2 cups of water until soft and fully cooked. Set aside. You can skip this step if you want to make sangati without rice.
In a large pot, bring the remaining 2 cups of water to a boil. Add salt to taste.
Lower the heat and gradually sprinkle the ragi flour into the boiling water while stirring continuously to avoid lumps. If you've added rice, you can mix it in at this stage.
Stir the mixture well and cook it over low heat for about 10-15 minutes, until the flour is fully cooked and the mixture becomes thick.
Once the mixture reaches a thick, dough-like consistency, remove it from the heat. Wet your hands with water and shape the sangati into balls or serve as is.

recipes.name: Rasgulla
instructions: Boil the milk in a heavy-bottomed pan.
Once it starts boiling, lower the heat and add lemon juice gradually while stirring.
When the milk curdles completely, turn off the heat.
Strain the curdled milk using a muslin cloth or fine strainer.
Rinse with cold water to remove the lemon taste and squeeze out excess water.
Hang the chhena for 30 minutes to remove excess moisture.
Place the chhena on a clean surface and knead it with your palm for 8-10 minutes until it becomes smooth and soft.
Divide it into small equal-sized balls and roll them smoothly without cracks.
In a deep pan, add sugar and water, and bring it to a boil.
Add cardamom pods for flavor (optional).
Once the sugar syrup is boiling, gently drop the chhena balls into it.
Cover the pan and let them cook for 15-20 minutes on medium heat.
They will double in size as they cook.
Turn off the heat and let them cool in the syrup.
Add rose water for extra flavor (optional).
Refrigerate for a few hours before serving.

recipes.name: sambar recipe
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (carrot, drumstick, pumpkin, brinjal, beans, etc.)
instructions: Rinse toor dal and pressure cook with 2 cups water, turmeric, and a few drops of oil for 3-4 whistles until soft.
Mash the cooked dal and set aside.
In a separate pot, cook chopped vegetables with 2 cups water until soft.
Add tamarind pulp, salt, and sambar powder. Simmer for 5 minutes
Add mashed dal to the cooked vegetables.
Mix well and let it simmer for 5-7 minutes. Adjust water and salt if needed.
Heat oil or ghee in a small pan.
Add mustard seeds and cumin seeds; let them splutter.
Add dry red chilies, curry leaves, and asafoetida. Stir for a few seconds.
Pour the tempering over the sambar and mix well.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with rice, idli, dosa, or vada.

recipes.name: vegetable sandwich
ingredients: 4 slices of bread (white, whole wheat, or multigrain)
instructions: Wash and thinly slice all vegetables.
Grate carrot if using.
Butter the bread slices evenly.
Spread green chutney on one side (optional).
Place a layer of cucumber, tomato, onion, and other veggies on one slice of bread.
Sprinkle salt, black pepper, and chaat masala over the veggies.
Add cheese or mayonnaise if desired.
Cover with another slice of bread.
Serve as a fresh sandwich orGrill/toast in a sandwich maker or pan for 2-3 minutes until crispy and golden.
Cut into halves or triangles.
Serve with ketchup or extra green chutney.

recipes.name: Banana Bread
ingredients: 1 ¾ cups (220g) all-purpose flour (or whole wheat flour for a healthier version)
½ cup (120ml) vegetable oil (or melted butter)
½ cup (100g) brown sugar (or white sugar)
½ cup chopped walnuts or pecans
2 tablespoons honey or maple syrup (for extra sweetness)
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F).
Grease a loaf pan with butter or line it with parchment paper.
In a bowl, whisk together flour, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon.
In another bowl, mash bananas with a fork.
Add sugar, eggs, vanilla extract, and oil. Mix well.
Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet mixture.
Gently fold until combined (do not overmix).
Add nuts or chocolate chips if using.
Pour the batter into the greased loaf pan.
Bake for 50-60 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Let it cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.
Slice and enjoy!

recipes.name: Gongura chicken
ingredients: 2 tablespoons oil (mustard oil or any cooking oil)
½ cup water (as needed for gravy consistency)
1 ½ cups gongura leaves (sorrel leaves, washed and chopped)
instructions: Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a pan, add dried red chilies, garlic, and cumin seeds.
Add the washed and chopped gongura leaves and sauté until soft and wilted.
Let it cool and grind into a smooth paste. Set aside.
Heat oil in a pan, add chopped onions, and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, sauté until raw smell disappears.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder, and salt. Cook until tomatoes turn soft.
Add chicken pieces and cook for 5-7 minutes on medium heat.
Add water and cover; simmer for 15-20 minutes until chicken is tender.
Stir in the prepared gongura paste and mix well.
Cook for another 5 minutes to blend flavors.
Add garam masala and adjust salt if needed.
Heat oil in a small pan, add mustard seeds, curry leaves, and dried red chili.
Pour the tempering over the chicken curry and mix well.
Serve hot with steamed rice, roti, or jeera rice.

recipes.name: Jamaican Curry Chicken
ingredients: 1 Scotch bonnet pepper (chopped, optional for heat)
1/2 cup coconut milk (optional, for a creamier texture)
instructions: Wash the chicken with vinegar or lime juice and water, then drain.
Season with curry powder, salt, black pepper, thyme, paprika, garlic, ginger, onion, and green onion.
Let it marinate for at least 30 minutes (overnight for best flavor).
Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add 1 tbsp of curry powder to the oil and stir until fragrant (about 30 seconds).
Add the seasoned chicken to the pot and stir well to coat with the curry-infused oil.
Let it brown for about 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add tomatoes, Scotch bonnet pepper, potato, and carrot.
Pour in water or chicken broth until the chicken is just covered.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is tender.
If using coconut milk, add it in the last 10 minutes for a richer taste.
Adjust seasoning to taste.
Enjoy with steamed white rice, rice and peas, or roti.

recipes.name: pani puri
ingredients: 1 tbsp jaggery or sugar (optional, for balance)
instructions: Mix semolina, flour, salt, and water to form a stiff dough.
Cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Roll out small, thin circles and deep-fry in hot oil until they puff up.
Drain on paper towels and let them cool until crispy.
Blend mint, coriander, green chilies, ginger, tamarind, and spices into a paste.
Mix with cold water and strain. Adjust seasoning as needed.
Chill for at least 30 minutes for better flavor.
Mix mashed potatoes, chickpeas, and spices.
Adjust seasoning to taste.
Gently crack open a puri.
Fill with a small amount of potato-chickpea mixture.
Pour in the chilled spiced water.
Enjoy immediately!

recipes.name: Chilli Con Carne
ingredients: 1 lb (450g) ground beef (or a mix of beef and pork)
1 can (14 oz) kidney beans (drained and rinsed)
1 can (14 oz) black beans (optional, drained and rinsed)
1 tbsp chili powder (adjust for spice level)
1/2 tsp cayenne pepper (optional, for extra heat)
1 small piece of dark chocolate or 1 tsp cocoa powder (optional, for richness)
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add chopped onions and sauté for 2-3 minutes until soft.
Stir in garlic and bell pepper, cook for another 2 minutes.
Add ground beef and break it up with a spatula.
Cook until browned, about 5-7 minutes. Drain excess fat if needed.
Stir in chili powder, cumin, paprika, cayenne, oregano, salt, and black pepper.
Add tomato paste and mix well.
Pour in diced tomatoes and Worcestershire sauce.
Add beef broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30-45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in drained kidney beans (and black beans if using).
Add sugar and a small piece of dark chocolate (if using).
Simmer uncovered for another 15 minutes to thicken.
Serve hot with rice, tortilla chips, or bread.
Garnish with cheese, sour cream, and fresh herbs.

recipes.name: Saag Paneer
ingredients: 1/4 cup cream or yogurt (optional, for richness)
instructions: In a pot, boil spinach and mustard greens with green chili, salt, and 1/2 cup water for 5-7 minutes.
Let it cool slightly, then blend into a smooth or slightly coarse puree. Set aside.
Heat 1 tbsp oil or ghee in a pan.
Lightly fry the paneer cubes until golden brown on all sides. Set aside.
In the same pan, heat 1 tbsp ghee or oil.
Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
Stir in garlic, ginger, and tomato puree. Cook for 3-4 minutes.
Add turmeric, garam masala, coriander powder, and red chili powder. Mix well.
Pour the blended spinach into the pan and mix well.
Simmer for 5-7 minutes on low heat.
Stir in cream or yogurt (if using) for a rich texture.
Add fried paneer cubes and cook for 2 more minutes.
Adjust salt and add dried fenugreek leaves for extra flavor.
Garnish with butter or ghee and a squeeze of lemon.
Serve hot with naan, roti, or basmati rice.

recipes.name: Vada Pav
instructions: Prepare the Batata Vada (Potato Filling):
Heat oil in a pan and add mustard seeds. Let them splutter.
Add curry leaves, green chilies, ginger, and garlic. Sauté for 1 minute.
Add turmeric powder and mashed potatoes. Mix well.
Add salt, lemon juice, and coriander leaves. Mix thoroughly.
Allow the mixture to cool, then shape into small round balls.
In a bowl, mix gram flour, turmeric, chili powder, salt, and baking soda.
Add water gradually and whisk to make a smooth, thick batter.
Heat oil in a deep pan for frying.
Dip each potato ball in the gram flour batter, coating it completely.
Deep fry until golden brown and crispy. Drain on paper towels.
Slice the pav in half and toast with butter on a pan.
Spread dry garlic chutney (or green/tamarind chutney) on the pav.
Place a hot vada inside and press lightly.
Serve with fried green chilies and chutneys on the side.

recipes.name: Kheer
ingredients: 1/2 cup basmati rice (or any short-grain rice)
8-10 saffron strands (optional, soaked in warm milk)
instructions: Rinse rice 2-3 times in water and soak for 30 minutes.
Drain the rice before using.
In a heavy-bottomed pan, heat milk over medium heat until it starts boiling.
Add the drained rice and stir well to avoid sticking.
Cook on low heat for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the rice is soft and the milk thickens.
Add sugar and mix well until dissolved.
Stir in cardamom powder and saffron strands (if using).
Let the kheer simmer for another 5-7 minutes.
In a small pan, heat 1 tbsp ghee and roast cashews, almonds, and raisins until golden.
Add the roasted dry fruits to the kheer and mix well.
Serve warm or chilled, garnished with pistachios and extra saffron strands.

recipes.name: Pesarattu
instructions: Rinse and soak whole green gram (and rice, if using) in water for 6-8 hours or overnight.
Drain the water and blend with ginger, green chilies, cumin seeds, coriander leaves, and salt.
Add water gradually and blend into a smooth yet slightly thick batter.
Heat a non-stick or cast-iron tawa on medium heat.
Pour a ladle of batter and spread it in a circular motion like a dosa.
Drizzle oil around the edges and let it cook until golden brown.
Sprinkle chopped onions, green chilies, grated carrots, or coriander on top.
Press the toppings gently with a spatula and cook for another 1-2 minutes.
Flip the pesarattu (optional) and cook for another 30 seconds.
Serve hot with ginger chutney, coconut chutney, or upma.

recipes.name: Upma
instructions: Heat a dry pan on medium heat.
Add 1 cup semolina and dry roast for 3-4 minutes, stirring continuously until it turns slightly golden and aromatic.
Transfer to a plate and set aside.
Heat 2 tbsp oil or ghee in a pan.
Add mustard seeds and let them splutter.
Add urad dal & chana dal and sauté until golden.
Add green chilies, ginger, chopped onions, and curry leaves. Sauté for 2 minutes.
Add chopped vegetables (if using) and cook for 2 more minutes.
Add 2 cups water to the pan and bring it to a boil.
Slowly add the roasted semolina, stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Add salt & turmeric powder (if using).
Stir and cook on low heat for 3-4 minutes, until the upma thickens and absorbs the water.
Turn off the heat, cover, and let it sit for 2 minutes.
Add lemon juice & chopped coriander leaves.
Serve hot with coconut chutney or pickle.

recipes.name: Spaghetti Carbonara
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, pecorino, and parmesan cheese.
Cook the pancetta in a large pan until crispy.
Drain the spaghetti and reserve some pasta water.
Toss the spaghetti with the pancetta, then remove from heat and mix in the egg mixture.
Add reserved pasta water to adjust the sauce consistency.
Season with black pepper and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Creamy chicken Carbonara
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook linguine al dente. Reserve 1/2 cup of pasta water before straining.
Combine eggs, Parmesan cheese, a pinch of salt, and pepper, and optional cream in a medium-sized bowl (image 2a). Whisk thoroughly and set aside (image 2b).

Meanwhile, cook bacon in a large stainless pan or cast iron skillet on medium heat until fully cooked, remove from the skillet, and place on a paper towel-lined plate to drain. Keep 1-2 tablespoons of bacon grease in the skillet and discard the rest.

Add sliced chicken. Season with salt and pepper and cook until chicken is fully cooked through (about 5-7 minutes). The bacon fat should brown the chicken. In the last 1-2 minutes, add garlic and a pinch of olive oil. Cook until fragrant.

Turn the heat down to low and let the pan cool for 2-3 minutes. Remove from the heat if necessary. (If the pan is too hot, you’ll run the risk of scrambling the eggs.) Return the bacon to the pan and add the warm linguine. Add the egg mixture to the pan along with 1/4 cup of pasta water (image 5a). Toss with the pasta until fully mixed and creamy. Add more pasta water if the sauce feels too thick (image 5b).
Top with fresh basil and serve immediately with extra Parmesan cheese and garnish with fresh basil.

recipes.name: Chicken biryani
ingredients: A blend of whole spices like cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, cumin seeds, turmeric, garam masala
fresh herbs like cilantro and mint
other additions might include green chilies, fried onions, and bay leaves
instructions: Make the marinade by mixing yogurt, ginger, garlic, turmeric, red chili powder, garam masala, salt, mint leaves, and lemon juice.
Add chicken and coat evenly with the marinade. Keep in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. You can marinate the chicken overnight too.
While the chicken is marinating, rinse and drain the rice 2 to 3 times, then soak in water for 20 minutes.
While the rice is soaking, add ghee to a heavy-bottomed pan and add onions.

On medium heat, fry the onions stirring frequently until they start to turn golden brown - about 15 to 20 minutes. Remove the fried onions from the pan, leaving the excess ghee behind as we will use this pan to cook the chicken.
In a medium pot add 8 cups of water. Add cumin seeds, bay leaves, star anise, cardamom, cloves, and salt to the rice and bring the to a boil on high heat.

Drain the soaked rice and add it to the boiling water. Bring the rice to a full boil on high heat. Lower the heat to medium and cook uncovered for 5 to 6 minutes or until the rice is about 90% cooked. Drain the rice promptly and reserve.
To the pan with the remaining ghee, add the marinated chicken. Cook on medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning halfway through.Then, gently layer the partially cooked rice over the chicken

Top with caramelized onions and saffron-infused milk.Cover the pot and seal it with aluminum foil, then place some weight on top of the lid. Cook on low heat for 20 minutes, this is the steam or Dum cooking step. Turn the heat off and wait another 10 minutes before opening the pot.In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, pecorino, and parmesan cheese.

recipes.name: Chicken Shawarma
instructions: Combine the marinade ingredients in a large ziplock bag. Add the chicken, seal, the massage from the outside with your hands to make sure each piece is coated. Marinate 24 hours (minimum 3 hours).
Combine the Yogurt Sauce ingredients in a bowl and mix. Cover and put in the fridge until required (it will last for 3 days in the fridge).
Heat a large non-stick skillet with 1 tablespoon over medium high heat, or lightly brush a BBQ hotplate/grills with oil and heat to medium high.
Place chicken in the skillet or on the grill and cook the first side for 4 to 5 minutes until nicely charred. Turn and cook the other side for 3 to 4 minutes (the 2nd side takes less time).
Remove chicken from the grill and cover loosely with foil. Set aside to rest for 5 minutes.
Slice chicken and pile onto platter alongside flatbreads, Salad and the Yoghurt Sauce.
To make a wrap, get a piece of flatbread and smear with Yoghurt Sauce. Top with a bit of lettuce and tomato and Chicken Shawarma. Roll up and enjoy!.

recipes.name: Veg Pizza
ingredients: vegetables(Bell peppers, Broccoli, Cauliflower, Carrots, Mushrooms, Onions, Olives, Paneer, Pineapple, and Tomatoes)
Other ingredients(garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, oregano, and basil)
instructions: Sprinkle yeast over warm water in a small bowl. The water should be no more than 100 degrees F (40 degrees C). Let stand for 5 minutes until yeast softens and begins to form a creamy foam.

Sift flour, sugar, 1 tablespoon oregano, and 1 teaspoon salt into a large bowl. Mix egg and oil into dry ingredients; stir in yeast mixture. When dough has pulled together, turn out onto a lightly floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic, about 8 minutes. Lightly oil a large bowl, then place dough in bowl and turn to coat with oil. Cover with a light cloth and let rise in a warm place (80 to 95 degrees F (27 to 35 degrees C)) until doubled in volume, about 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 450 degrees F (235 degrees C). Lightly grease a baking sheet.

Cook and stir diced tomatoes, tomato paste, onion, 1 tablespoon oregano, garlic, onion powder, 1 teaspoon salt, and pepper in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook until sauce has thickened, 15 to 20 minutes.

Punch down dough and turn it out onto a lightly floured surface. Use a knife to divide dough into two equal pieces--do not tear. Shape dough into rounds and let rest for 10 minutes. Form dough into rectangles, and place onto prepared baking sheet. Spoon tomato sauce over dough. Sprinkle with 1 1/4 cup mozzarella cheese; top with bell pepper, onion, and mushroom. Sprinkle 1/4 cup mozzarella cheese over top.
Bake in preheated oven until crust is browned and crisp and cheese has melted, 20 to 25 minutes.

recipes.name: Chicken Lollipop
ingredients: Ginger-garlic paste or minced ginger and garlic
Red chili powder, red chili sauce, or red chili paste
Green chili peppers or spring onions
instructions: Whisk together the sauce ingredients in a bowl
Coat the chicken with the sauce or spice mix and flour or cornstarch
Heat oil in a pan or skillet for deep frying
Drop the coated chicken into the hot oil in batches
Fry until the chicken is crispy and golden brown
Remove from oil and place on a plate

recipes.name: Chocolate chip cookies
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
In a bowl, cream together softened butter, brown sugar, and white sugar.
Beat in eggs one at a time, then stir in vanilla extract.
Combine flour, baking soda, and salt. Gradually add to the wet ingredients.
Fold in chocolate chips.
Drop rounded tablespoons of dough onto ungreased baking sheets.
Bake for 10-12 minutes or until edges are golden brown.
Allow cookies to cool on the baking sheet for a few minutes before transferring to a wire rack.

recipes.name: Gobi Manchurian
ingredients: Other ingredients(vegetable stock, ketchup, chile-garlic sauce, and green onion)
instructions: Clean the cauliflower and cut into small florets.Parboil or blanch by keeping it immersed in boiling hot water with salt for 15-20 minutes.
Make a batter with corn flour, all purpose flour and cooking soda if adding, thick enough to coat the cauliflowers.
You can either dip the well drained florets one by one in the batter or just mix all of it with the drained florets and deep fry.
Just make sure there is enough batter to coat the florets. Deep fry until crisp and light. Keep aside.
In a wide pan, add 3 tablespoon oil and add chopped garlic, chilli if adding.
Give a quick stir and then add finely chopped white part of the spring onion and the chopped onion and fry till transparent. I added colored capsicum too, just 2 tablespoon each.
Add both sauces, salt a little bit, sugar if adding, pepper and mix well.
Add the deep fried cauliflower florets and toss well to mix it evenly. Lastly add finely chopped green part of the spring onion and mix well for a minute.
Mix corn flour, vinegar in water.Add to the cauliflower, mix in high flame. Once you see a glaze and becomes shiny, switch off flame.

recipes.name: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
instructions: Marinate chicken thighs in a mixture of yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, garam masala, and Kashmiri red chili powder.
In a pan, melt butter and sauté the marinated chicken until browned.
Add tomato puree and cook until the oil separates. Stir in heavy cream.
Sprinkle kasuri methi, sugar, and salt. Simmer until the chicken is fully cooked.
Serve this creamy butter chicken over rice or with naan for an authentic Pakistani/Indian experience.

recipes.name: Mango Lassi
instructions: In a blender, combine diced mango, yogurt, milk, honey, and cardamom powder.
Blend until smooth and creamy.
Add ice cubes and blend again until the lassi is chilled.
Pour into glasses and garnish with a sprinkle of cardamom.
Enjoy this refreshing Mango Lassi!

recipes.name: Blueberry Banana Smoothie
instructions: In a blender, combine blueberries, banana, Greek yogurt, almond milk, and honey.
Blend until smooth and creamy.
Add chia seeds for extra nutrition and blend briefly.
Pour into a glass and enjoy this nutritious Blueberry Banana Smoothie!

recipes.name: South Indian Masala Dosa
ingredients: Dosa batter (fermented rice and urad dal batter)
instructions: In a pan, heat ghee and add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and curry leaves.
Add chopped onions, green chilies, and turmeric powder. Sauté until onions are golden brown.
Mix in boiled and mashed potatoes. Cook until well combined and seasoned.
Spread dosa batter on a hot griddle to make thin pancakes.
Place a spoonful of the potato mixture in the center, fold, and serve hot.
Pair with coconut chutney for a delicious South Indian meal.

recipes.name: Pav Bhaji
ingredients: Vegetables(potatoes, peas, tomatoes, cauliflower, cabbage, carrots, or beans)
Spices(red chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin-coriander powder)
instructions: Boil the vegetables
Mash the vegetables
Heat oil and butter in a pan
Add chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste
Add chopped capsicum and tomato
Add spices
Add water
Add mashed vegetables and lemon juice
Serve with pav

recipes.name: Gobi Fries Rice
ingredients: Vegetables(Carrots, onions, beans, cabbage, capsicum, and peas are common additions)
Seasonings(Chili powder, garam masala, coriander powder, ginger garlic paste, soy sauce, red chili sauce, and pepper)
Other ingredients(Corn flour, maida, lemon juice, curd, and coriander leaves)
instructions: Mix all the ingredients to coat Cauliflower into a thick paste.
Put the Cauliflower pieces in the mixture and let the florets be coated well.

Put the coated pieces in boiling Oil and fry until they turn golden brown on a medium flame. When they turn golden, turn the flame to high and fry until they are crisp. (Check the tips on how to fry them to perfection).
Heat Oil and add Red Chillies, Curry Leaves and Garlic and fry.
Add chopped Onions, Green Chillies and fry until the Onions are cooked.
Add the Onions and the rest of the ingredients in the Rice and toss on a high flame.
Before you take it off the fire, add the fried Cauliflower florets and toss on a high flame.
Garnish with Green Coriander and serve hot.

recipes.name: Dry Fruit Laddu
instructions: Firstly, in a pan heat 1 tsp ghee. roast 1 cup badam, ½ cup cashew and ¼ cup pistachios.
Roast until the nuts turn crunchy. Keep aside.
In the same pan heat 1 tsp ghee, add ½ cup raisins and 6 anjeer.
Dry roast 3 tbsp pumpkin seeds, 3 tbsp sunflower seeds, 2 tbsp sesame, 1 tbsp poppy seeds, and 1 cup dry coconut.
Roast until the seeds turn crunchy. Keep aside.
Mix all the roasted nuts and seeds well. Keep aside.
In a large kadai heat 2 tbsp ghee. add 350 grams dates and cook on low flame.
After 5 minutes, the dates turn soft and mushy. Mash the dates until it turns paste texture.
Now add in roasted nuts and mix well.
Mix until everything is well combined.
Cool slightly, and start shaping into ladoo.
Finally, Dry Fruits Ladoo is ready to enjoy for up to a month.

recipes.name: Mothichor Laddu
ingredients: Nuts like pistachios or chopped nuts
instructions: Mix the ingredients together.
Fry the gram flour batter into small balls called boondis.
Boil sugar and water with a little lemon juice to prevent crystallization.
Add food coloring and mix.
Combine the boondis with the sugar syrup.
Cool and shape into ladoos.

recipes.name: Chicken Kebab
ingredients: Lemon Juice. Or apple cider vinegar.
Bell Peppers. Or other veggies of choice.
instructions: Place the chicken pieces in a large bowl and add the olive oil, garlic, soy sauce, oregano, green and red bell peppers, and lemon juice (or lemon zest). Mix everything well. Cover, and refrigerate for between 2 to 24 hours to let it marinate.
Preheat the grill to medium-high heat. Arrange the chicken and peppers onto the skewers and lay them on a baking sheet to take out to the hot grill.
Oil the grill grates. Cook for about 7 minutes on each side, until the chicken is well done.

recipes.name: Mutton soup
instructions: Cut and wash the mutton pieces and take in pressure cooker.
Add two cups of water to it.
Add ginger garlic paste, salt, pepper powder, cumin powder and garam masala to it.
Mix together and close the pan.
Pressure cook for 5-6 whistles.
Once it cools down open the cooker, garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot.
Mutton soup is ready.

recipes.name: Mango Icecream
ingredients: Cream(whipping cream, fresh cream, or thickened cream)
Milk powder, to improve texture and reduce ice crystals
Corn flour, to thicken the ice cream
instructions: Puree the mangoes until smooth.
Combine the mango puree with the cream and sweetener.
Whisk or beat until combined.
Freeze until set

recipes.name: Brownie
instructions: First, mix together the dry and wet ingredients in two separate bowls. Combine the sugar, flour, powdered sugar, cocoa powder, chocolate chips, and salt in a medium bowl. Then, whisk together the eggs, olive oil, and water in a large one.
Next, combine the wet and dry ingredients. Sprinkle the dry mixture over the wet one, and fold until just combined. The batter will be thick!.

Then, pour the batter into an 8×8 inch baking pan lined with parchment paper. Use a rubber spatula to spread it to all four sides of the pan and to smooth the top. The mixture will be very thick – that’s ok.

Finally, bake! Transfer the pan to a 325-degree oven and bake for 40 to 45 minutes, until a toothpick inserted comes out with a few crumbs attached. Allow the brownies to cool completely before slicing and serving. Enjoy!

recipes.name: Fish Curry
ingredients: Fish fillets - 500 grams (any white fish like tilapia or basa)
Red chili powder - 1 teaspoon (adjust to taste)
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, pecorino, and parmesan cheese.
Cook the pancetta in a large pan until crispy.
Drain the spaghetti and reserve some pasta water.
Toss the spaghetti with the pancetta, then remove from heat and mix in the egg mixture.
Add reserved pasta water to adjust the sauce consistency.
Season with black pepper and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Tamarind Rice
instructions: Clean and wash the fish fillets. Sprinkle a little salt and turmeric powder on the fish and set aside.
Heat oil in a pan.
Add the chopped onions and sauté until soft and golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté for a minute until the raw smell goes away.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they soften and turn mushy.
Add turmeric powder, red chili powder, and coriander powder. Stir well.
Add water (and coconut milk if using) and bring to a boil.
Gently add the fish fillets to the curry. Let it simmer on low heat for 8-10 minutes, or until the fish is fully cooked.
Avoid stirring too much to keep the fish intact.
Once the fish is cooked, check the seasoning and add more salt if needed.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve with rice or roti.

recipes.name: Prawn Curry
ingredients: Red chili powder - 1 teaspoon (adjust to taste)
instructions: Clean and devein the prawns. Rinse them well.
Sprinkle a little salt and turmeric powder on the prawns and set aside.
Heat oil in a pan.
Add the chopped onions and sauté until they turn soft and golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté for a minute until the raw smell disappears.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they become mushy.
Add turmeric powder, red chili powder, and coriander powder. Mix well.
Add water (and coconut milk if using) and bring the curry to a gentle boil.
Add the prawns to the curry. Simmer for about 5-7 minutes, or until the prawns are fully cooked. Be careful not to overcook them as prawns cook quickly.
Taste the curry and adjust salt if needed.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with steamed rice or roti

recipes.name: Pootharekulu
ingredients: Rice paper wrappers (available at most stores) - 10 sheets
instructions: BIf using dry rice paper wrappers, lightly dampen them with a wet cloth to make them flexible and easy to work with.
Take one rice paper wrapper and place it on a flat surface.
Gently brush a thin layer of melted ghee over the entire sheet.
Sprinkle powdered sugar evenly on top of the ghee.
If desired, sprinkle some chopped nuts for added flavor and texture.
Fold the rice paper in thirds or roll it into a tight rectangle or burrito shape, making sure the layers are even.
Repeat the process for all the remaining rice paper wrappers.

recipes.name: Mango Pickle
ingredients: Raw mangoes - 2 medium (cut into small cubes)
instructions: Wash and dry the raw mangoes. Ensure there is no moisture.
Cut the mangoes into small cubes and set aside.
In a pan, dry roast mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds until they turn aromatic.
Once roasted, coarsely grind them into a powder and set aside.
In a mixing bowl, add the mango cubes.
Add red chili powder, turmeric powder, the ground mustard-fenugreek powder, and salt. Mix well.
Heat the oil in a small pan until it is smoking hot.
Turn off the heat and add a pinch of asafoetida (hing) to the oil.
Let the oil cool for a few minutes, then pour it over the mango-spice mixture. Mix everything thoroughly.
Let the pickle sit for 1-2 hours so the flavors blend.
Store the mango pickle in a clean, dry, airtight jar. You can start enjoying it right away, but it tastes even better after a couple of days as the flavors deepen.

recipes.name: Rotis
ingredients: Oil or ghee - 1 teaspoon (optional, for softer rotis)
instructions: Mix dough: In a bowl, combine 2 cups wheat flour with a little water and knead until soft.
Rest dough: Let the dough rest for 15 minutes.
Divide and roll: Make small dough balls, flatten them, and roll into thin circles.
Cook roti: Heat a pan, cook each roti on both sides until it puffs up and gets light brown spots.
Serve: Serve hot with ghee or butter.
